package.title: Tirzepatide: Why You May Feel Full Before Thanksgiving Dinner #shorts
package.description:
Tirzepatide's label may help explain feeling full before Thanksgiving dinner even starts. The label says tirzepatide decreases calorie intake, likely by affecting appetite, and slows stomach emptying. That delay is largest after the first dose, and it diminishes over time. Tip 1: tasting while cooking counts as part of the meal. Tip 2: plate your favorites to enjoy later, once you have room.
Low blood sugar risk may be higher if you take insulin or a sulfonylurea, and it has also been reported in adults without type 2 diabetes.
If you get severe stomach pain that will not go away, with or without vomiting, stop using tirzepatide and call your healthcare provider right away. For anything that isn't that emergency sign, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.
#Tirzepatide
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

script.cta: Spoken close: "Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber. Next time you're full before dinner, remember:" This loops back into sentence 1. There is no subscribe line and no description-link line. Post notes: 159 spoken words, counted by hand after every fact-check fix (standard arm, 135–160). By scene: s01 12, s02 16, s03 21, s04 17, s05 12, s06 26, s07 41, s08 14. To stay under 160, we cut "surprises people" from s05 (−2), changed "Then add" to "Plus" in s04 (−1) and changed "while you cook" to "while cooking" (−1). These offset the +3 in s03 and the +1 "may be" in s06. Fixes applied: the s02 card names the drug and uses the label's verb; the s03 narration says "The label also says", and its card adds the drug and "largest after first dose"; s06 now says "may be higher"; the s07 red-flag card is split into two fixed cards. Sources now use the fact-checker's verified DailyMed label (src1) and Lilly's clinician page (src2). s02 is tagged to src2, where the calorie-intake and appetite wording was verified. Cards: s03, s06 and s07 use fixed, pre-split cards separated by " | ". Never run them through the auto-splitter. Exp G target long video: Thanksgiving. This Short covers feeling full while cooking, before dinner, so it doesn't repeat the S3 11-22 'morning after' holiday Short.

factcheck.summary: Content check of the Thanksgiving tirzepatide Short (standard length). The label facts are accurate and hedged. I confirmed against the Zepbound label (DailyMed, revised 28 Aug 2026) that tirzepatide delays stomach emptying, that the delay is largest after the first dose, and that it diminishes over time. Lilly's own page for clinicians confirms it lowers calorie intake, likely by affecting appetite. The DailyMed text I could read confirms that section 5.7 exists and that tirzepatide can cause low blood sugar, with the risk going up alongside insulin secretagogues. I couldn't extract the exact wording on insulin, sulfonylureas and adults without type 2 diabetes. The script's line matches our house scope note for section 5.7. The pancreatitis line keeps "stop using tirzepatide", "call your healthcare provider right away" and "with or without vomiting", as the tirzepatide rule requires. The DailyMed extract paraphrased this part of the Medication Guide, so I couldn't match the exact sentence. The don't-stop line uses the single-sign wording correctly. The closing safety line is present, and there's no subscribe line and no description-link line. I hand-counted 159 spoken words (12+16+18+19+14+25+41+14), which matches the post notes and fits the 135–160 arm. The hook's "may help explain" hedge is honest, and s04 openly names tasting and appetizers as other reasons for feeling full. The tips are our own, and they're gentle and non-restrictive. The remaining issues are minor wording fixes to the on-screen cards and one hedge. The src1 URL (pi.lilly.com) opens, but its PDF text can't be extracted. I verified the facts on DailyMed instead and list that, plus Lilly's clinician page, as the verified sources.
